MOUNT MAUNGANUI: For Naman Dhir, earning an India cap was never the finish line. The 26-year-old all-rounder believes his real journey has only just begun. In an exclusive conversation with TOI, Dhir spoke about his rapid rise, the challenges of life in international cricket, his bowling transformation, and his dream of featuring in the 2027 ODI World Cup.Everything happened at a rapid pace. It has now. The call-up itself came as a surprise. I had no idea I would be picked for the West Indies ODIs, so it took a couple of days to sink in. Once I joined the team, though, everything felt normal. I’m also happy that we managed to win both the ODI and T20I series in New Zealand. I was performing whenever opportunities came my way and had already played a few IPL seasons in flexible roles. I always believed the chance would come when the time was right.Not at all. It came completely out of the blue. I had just returned from the tournament and was unpacking my whites to prepare for the Ranji Trophy when I saw the squad announcement on Instagram.Playing for India is every cricketer’s dream, but for me, the job is far from done.I want to play for a long time and win matches for India. I don’t set specific targets. My focus is on contributing to victories and remaining part of the team for as long as possible.I’ve always bowled, but my understanding improved significantly after joining Mumbai Indians . Working with quality coaches and players, especially Rahul Sanghvi sir, helped me understand the craft much better. Over the last two to three years, I’ve increased my workload and made technical changes, including using my body and shoulder more effectively.You definitely need both. Modern white-ball cricket is demanding because almost any target feels chaseable. You have to be brave, but you also need a clear plan. It’s about knowing when to bowl a defensive delivery, when to concede a single, and when to attack for a wicket.Sharing a dressing room with players like Rohit Sharma, Hardik Pandya and Suryakumar Yadav felt surreal. For the first few days, I was hesitant, wondering how to approach them. But everyone made me feel welcome. I developed a very close bond with Hardik bhai. We discussed batting extensively, and those conversations helped me settle in quickly.Absolutely. It’s not just about walking in and swinging from ball one. But I enjoy the challenge. Honestly, I’m happy batting anywhere. Even openers have to attack these days. If you’re coming in around the 15th or 16th over, you usually get a few deliveries to assess conditions before looking to accelerate. If you stay calm and make smart decisions, the role becomes easier.He’s very clear. He wants players to be switched on, make smart decisions and give everything on the field. Even if you score a hundred, you’ll get a pat on the back and then be challenged to do even better in the next game.Absolutely. Red-ball cricket will always remain a priority for me. Before the India call-up, I was preparing for the Ranji Trophy and had set myself the goal of scoring big runs. I believe that if you perform consistently in the longest format, every other format becomes easier.
Article Summary: The 26-year-old all-rounder believes his real journey has only just begun. Dhir spoke about his rapid rise, the challenges of life in international cricket, his bowling transformation, and his dream of featuring in the 2027 ODI World Cup.

Article Title: Three LA 2028 quotas at first attempt! India make best start to Olympic shooting cycle in decades
Article Text:
Jaypal Malviya

Three LA 2028 quotas at first attempt

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian shooters dominate ISSF People's Choice Awards race

NEW DELHI: India have made their strongest start to an Olympic qualification cycle in shooting in at least 16 years, securing three quota places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics at the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha, Qatar.For the first time across five consecutive Olympic cycles, stretching from London 2012 to LA28, Indian shooters have secured three Olympic quotas at the very first qualification event. The landmark achievement, made possible by podium finishes across all three shooting disciplines — rifle, pistol and shotgun — has given India an early advantage in the race for Olympic berths.Jaypal Malviya opened India's account with a silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol event. Niraj Kumar followed with bronze in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions, before Vivaan Kapoor completed the impressive haul with silver in the men's trap.The three podium finishes not only secured India's first Olympic quotas for LA28 but also underlined the growing depth across the country's shooting programme.India's Doha performance represents a significant improvement on its opening-event returns in the previous four Olympic qualification cycles.The country secured two quotas at the 2010 Munich World Championships ahead of London 2012, followed by just one at the 2014 Granada World Championships before the Rio 2016 Games.The tally improved to two at the 2018 Changwon World Championships ahead of Tokyo 2020, while India collected two quotas from the 2022 Osijek Shotgun World Championships and Cairo Rifle/Pistol World Championships before Paris 2024.The three quotas in Doha in 2026 have therefore set a new benchmark for India's opening performance in an Olympic qualification campaign since the London 2012 cycle.Welcoming the achievement, National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) president Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo said: "Starting an Olympic cycle with three quotas right at the first World Championship is a huge boost for everyone involved. What makes me happiest is that all three disciplines—rifle, pistol and shotgun—delivered podium finishes. Usually, it takes a few World Cups for the momentum to build, so getting three spots on the board this early takes a lot of pressure off the team and gives our coaching staff a clear runway to plan for Los Angeles. "NRAI secretary general Pawankumar Singh also praised the shooters for delivering under pressure against a strong international field."Winning a quota at a World Championship is never easy because every top shooter in the world is competing in the same field. Jaypal, Niraj and Vivaan kept their composure in very tight finals and earned those spots the hard way. Our high-performance team and coaches put in months of quiet work behind the scenes to get us here, and we will keep building on this start over the next two years," he said.India also finished second in the overall medal standings in Doha with 13 medals, comprising two gold, seven silver and four bronze, further underlining the strength of its campaign.India's impressive showing in international shooting has extended beyond the competition arena, with the country's shooters emerging as frontrunners in the ISSF 2026 Athlete of the Year People's Choice Awards.Four Indian shooters — Esha Singh, Elavenil Valarivan, Tilottama Sen and Sakshi Padekar — feature among the five nominees in the women's category, while Tushar Mane is leading the men's voting.Voting, which began on November 9, will close on November 18, with the winners in the men's and women's categories to be announced thereafter.
Article Summary: India secure three quota places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics at the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha, Qatar. The landmark achievement was made possible by podium finishes across all three shooting disciplines — rifle, pistol and shotgun. Jaypal Malviya opened India's account with a silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol event.

Article Title: Sandpapergate row | 'He was shocked': Usman Khawaja reveals why he kept David Warner in the dark
Article Text:
Usman Khawaja and David Warner (AFP Photo)

Khawaja feared news would spread among players

Warner backs Khawaja's account

Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has revealed that David Warner had no idea he was writing about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal until two months before his autobiography, Sabr, was published.Khawaja said he had promised Warner in 2020 that he would eventually speak about the controversy. However, the two barely discussed the issue over the next few years.He finally informed Warner about the book two months before its release. Khawaja said Warner was surprised to learn that he had written about the scandal."I had promised him for ages, because he's had to carry this for eight years. I didn't tell David Warner what was in my book until two months ago," Khawaja said while speaking on the They Used To Be... podcast."There's a period of time from 2020 when I sent a text message to 2026, where we barely discussed it - but I made a promise to him in 2020 and I stuck to it. I text him two months ago and he had no idea I was writing it, he was shocked. I was fighting with what I was gonna put in the book the whole time," he added.Warner reportedly received the chapter only a week before the book was published.Khawaja said he did not want his plans to become public before he was ready.He feared that word would spread quickly if he discussed the book with too many people."I didn't want it to get leaked - there are no secrets in cricket... once you say something it goes around the whole team and squad," he said.He also did not want to approach Warner while Australia were touring South Africa."I was just worried and the guys were going on a South African tour, I didn't want to do it while they were over there. So I just kept holding back, holding back. Then I thought, "There are two months until my book release and I have got to tell him"."Khawaja said his promise to Warner was one of the reasons he eventually decided to put his account in the book.Warner has since publicly supported Khawaja following the publication of the book.Khawaja's account has reignited the debate over the 2018 Cape Town Test, when Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball. Smith and Warner were handed 12-month bans by Cricket Australia, while Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.In his book, Khawaja has claimed that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was more widespread within Australia's touring party than Cricket Australia's investigation found. Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc have denied knowing that sandpaper would be used on the ball. Former batting coach Graeme Hick has also denied prior knowledge.Former teammate Chadd Sayers has also supported parts of Khawaja's account.
Article Summary: Usman Khawaja reveals that David Warner had no idea he was writing about the ball-tampering scandal. The former Australia opener revealed that he only told Warner two months before his autobiography, Sabr, was published. He said he had promised Warner in 2020 that he would eventually speak about the controversy. The two barely discussed the issue over the next few years.

Article Title: Daman U-turn fails to lift cloud over Kalyan Chaubey’s AIFF future
Article Text:
All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey

Panaji:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The newly-elected committee of the Daman and Diu Football Association has offered All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey a lifeline by submitting a new list of delegates for next month’s all-important general body meeting and elections.Outgoing Daman FA president Amit Khemani had named general secretary Walter Pereira and technical director Altamash Shaikh as the two delegates. The list was emailed to AIFF electoral officer Rajeev Sharma before the deadline of Nov 13.However, after Pereira, a former Mumbai-based referee and match commissioner, was elected unopposed as president on Saturday, Daman sent a new list to AIFF.“The new list, sent after the deadline, has the names of Pereira and Kalyan Chaubey,” a senior official told TOI. “The electoral officer has not taken a decision on the delegates from Daman since elections were pending until the cut-off date. A decision is likely to be taken later, in accordance with the AIFF constitution.”According to sources, elections in Daman have also come under scrutiny for not adhering to the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, largely due to absence of a mandatory Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) list and the size of its executive committee.Newly-elected president Pereira did not respond to calls and messages.Sharma, on Sunday, cleared the delegate list from 29 states while the fate of states where elections are held beyond the deadline, like Daman, Pondicherry FA, Uttarakhand State FA, Jammu & Kashmir FA, and Indian Football Association (West Bengal), hangs in the balance.According to the official delegate list, former AIFF president Praful Patel will represent WIFA at the general body and is eligible to contest elections.According to Sharma, “any intimation received after this deadline (of Sept 13), and any change in the names after it, shall be permitted only with the approval of the electoral officer, in accordance with Article 4.2 of Schedule III of the Constitution.”
Article Summary: The Daman and Diu Football Association has offered All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey a lifeline by submitting a new list of delegates. Outgoing Daman FA president Amit Khemani had named general secretary Walter Pereira and technical director Altamash Shaikh as the two delegates. The list was emailed to AIFF electoral officer Rajeev Sharma before the deadline of Nov 13.

Article Title: 'Iceman': Sunil Gavaskar compares Mohit Ulva to MS Dhoni after U19 Asia Cup final heroics
Article Text:
Sunil Gavaskar and MS Dhoni

Gavaskar Compares Ulva To MS Dhoni

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gavaskar Recalls Dhoni's 2011 World Cup Moment

Legendary Indian cricketer Sunil Gavaskar has praised young batter Mohit Ulva for his match-winning performance against Pakistan in the U19 Asia Cup 2026 final. Gavaskar compared Ulva's calmness under pressure to former India captain MS Dhoni after the youngster helped India pull off an incredible victory.India were chasing a target of 338 but looked almost certain to lose after slipping to 252/8.However, lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva turned the match around by scoring the runs needed in the final eight overs.Coming in at No. 10, Ulva played a stunning unbeaten knock of 49 runs from just 26 balls. His innings included five fours and three sixes. With three runs needed off the final delivery, he stepped out and hit a boundary over extra cover to seal India's victory.Gavaskar was impressed by the youngster's ability to stay calm in such a tense situation and compared his finishing skills to Dhoni."He (Ulva) showed coolness like MS Dhoni. Iceman. He just came out, hit a four, and saw. The non-striker was very happy. He took his helmet off, kept it down, and then raised his hands," Gavaskar said on Sony Sports.Gavaskar also compared Ulva's winning shot and celebration to Dhoni's famous six that sealed India's victory in the 2011 ODI World Cup final."Had MS Dhoni been there, he would have done like that too. You have seen the way MS Dhoni raised his bat after hitting the six in the World Cup. It's memorable, and this is also memorable," Gavaskar added.He also praised the Indian youngsters for refusing to give up despite losing eight wickets while chasing a big target."The biggest thing was that they never gave up. The score was 252 when the eighth wicket fell. More than 80 runs were required for a win. However, they kept their target in front of them," he added.
Article Summary: Mohit Ulva played a stunning unbeaten knock of 49 runs from just 26 balls. His innings included five fours and three sixes. With three runs needed off the final delivery, he stepped out and hit a boundary. Gavaskar was impressed by the youngster's ability to stay calm in such a tense situation.

Article Title: Complaint alleges irregularities in GFI camp funds, treasurer rejects charges
Article Text:
Gymnastics Federation of India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: A complaint submitted to the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Sunday has accused the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI) of possible diversion and misappropriation of govt funds released for national coaching camps in Bhubaneswar, alleging that athletes, coaches and vendors are yet to receive payments despite the federation submitting a utilisation certificate (UC) for the expenditure.In a representation to SAI, a copy of which is with TOI, former international gymnast and GFI general body member Rakesh Kumar Patra alleged that a little more than Rs 14.42 lakh sanctioned for men’s and women’s artistic gymnastics camps held ahead of the Asian Championships was shown as utilised, even though several liabilities remain unsettled.The complaint by the national coach claims that hospitality provider Swastik Hospitality is owed nearly Rs 12 lakh, while physiotherapist Yash Jaiswal and several gymnasts and coaches, including Dipa Karmakar, are awaiting reimbursements.Seeking an independent financial and vigilance inquiry, Patra has also sought scrutiny of GFI president Sudhir Mital, treasurer Kaushik Bidiwala and the chartered accountant firm Narender Singh & Co., which certified the utilisation certificate.Responding to the allegations, Bidiwala denied any irregularity in the issuance of the utilisation certificate. “A utilisation certificate cannot be issued without proper documentation and supporting records.If the documents are not available, even the chartered accountant will not certify it,” Bidwala told TOI.He said allegations and certification of expenditure were separate matters and maintained that the UC process involved verification of original documents and proofs.On the issue of pending reimbursements, Bidiwala said delays, if any, could be linked to procedural requirements rather than withholding of payments. “If any reimbursements are pending, it is not because there is an intention to withhold anyone’s money. There may be processing delays, but the money will not be stopped and beneficiaries will receive their payments,” he said.The treasurer added that he was focused on the welfare of the sport and cautioned that prolonged disputes could hurt gymnastics’ image and discourage parents from encouraging children to take up the discipline.
Article Summary: Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI) accused of possible diversion and misappropriation of govt funds released for national coaching camps in Bhubaneswar. Former international gymnast and GFI general body member Rakesh Kumar Patra alleged that a little more than Rs 14.42 lakh was shown as utilised.

Article Title: Indian lawn bowlers ready for New Zealand challenge after landmark year
Article Text:
(From left) Sunil Bahadur, Reshma Kumari, Pinki Singh and Dinesh Kumar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: It has been a good year for Indian lawn bowls. Putul Sonowal won bronze at the Champion of Champions tournament, India claimed four gold medals at the Asian Championships, and recently added a bronze in the mixed pairs event at the Malaysian Open.Perhaps more significantly, the Bowling Federation of India (BFI) received recognition from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports as the governing body for lawn bowls in the country. It was a major boost for the sport as it looks to build towards the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.Before that, however, the focus is on the Test series against New Zealand, scheduled for Nov 16, 17 and 18 in Auckland as part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two nations.Each Test will comprise five matches: men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2. India will be represented by Dinesh Kumar, Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh.Speaking about the opportunity, Dinesh, a five-time CWG participant, said: “Getting the opportunity to represent India in the Test series is a great moment for us.We are going there with the aim of delivering a strong performance.”Having trained together since 2008, Dinesh and Sunil have enjoyed a remarkable journey. The Ranchi-based duo now hopes to make the most of international competition as Indian lawn bowls continues to gain momentum on the global stage.“We are travelling regularly and gaining experience against some of the world’s best players. Every match becomes a learning opportunity. Even when we lose, we understand where we need to improve. Competing against experienced international players accelerates our development,” said Sunil, who partnered Reshma to win bronze in the mixed pairs event at the Malaysian Open earlier this month.The medal was a particularly significant achievement for Reshma, who was previously a 1500m runner but switched sports in 2023 after struggling with injuries. She is now eager to make the most of her upcoming tour to New Zealand.“Things are progressing well, my game is improving, and I am determined to take full advantage of every opportunity that comes my way,” said the youngster.While the players are pleased with the progress the sport has made in recent years, they believe India would benefit from hosting more invitational tournaments, similar to those regularly staged in established lawn bowls nations.BFI president Ravi Bengani shares that ambition. Having previously expressed confidence that India can challenge for as many as four gold medals at the 2030 Commonwealth Games, he is focused on creating more opportunities for players to gain exposure at the highest level.“Besides participating in international tournaments, we have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani had said.For now, however, the immediate challenge lies in Auckland, where India’s lawn bowlers will look to cap a landmark year by making a statement against New Zealand.
Article Summary: India's lawn bowlers will take on New Zealand in a Test series in Auckland. Dinesh Kumar, Sunil Bahadur, Reshma Kumari and Pinki Singh will represent India. The Test series is part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two nations.

Article Title: ‘Sacrifice runs for Virat Kohli’: Sunil Gavaskar's big take on pressure facing Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer
Article Text:
India's Virat Kohli

Mid-day

Legendary India batter Sunil Gavaskar has weighed in on the debate surrounding Virat Kohli 's pursuit of 100 international centuries, suggesting that a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well.Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74 off just 51 deliveries to guide India towards victory in a low-scoring contest. However, Gavaskar raised an interesting possibility in his latest column for: had Kohli stayed at the crease for longer, captain Shubman Gill and vice-captain Shreyas Iyer could have found themselves in a difficult position.With India closing in on the target, the two batters might have had to choose between finishing the match quickly and giving Kohli an opportunity to reach his century. The prospect becomes even more significant given that Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds.Gavaskar acknowledged that winning a match must remain the team's primary objective, but argued that helping a player achieve such a landmark, provided it does not compromise the result, could be a moment of collective celebration."Indians have always been fond of records and so there's always a debate about the rights and wrongs of going for it.One thing for sure that 99% of those who say they don't play for records are actually incapable talent and temperament wise of setting any and so it's easy for them to say so," Gavaskar wrote."There is not a single Indian cricket fan who does not want Kohli to get to 100 international centuries. We are all cheering for him to get there and so, if there's an occasion where some other teammate sacrifices his runs to allow him the chance to get there, the glory will not be just Kohli's but for all Indian cricket fans too," he added.Kohli eventually fell for 74 with India at 124/3 in the rain-affected contest, leaving the team with relatively little work to do in the chase. His dismissal also meant Gill and Iyer did not have to confront the possibility of managing the chase around his personal milestone.Gavaskar felt the two players were spared a potentially awkward situation, including the prospect of facing criticism from fans on social media if India had delayed sealing the victory to give Kohli a chance to complete his hundred."Kohli got out in the 70s. Gill and Iyer were thus spared any blowback if the winning runs had been hit with Kohli unbeaten in the 90s. Yes, it's a team game, but it's also good for the team if one of its members, especially a star player, gets to a personal milestone without affecting the team's chances of winning," Gavaskar pointed out.Kohli, who now plays only ODIs, has 86 international centuries to his name. He is chasing a landmark that remains exclusive to Sachin Tendulkar, the only batter to have scored 100 international hundreds.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds. Sunil Gavaskar says a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well. Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74.

From AC Milan and Barcelona to Ravenna's Serie C project

Brazil soccer star Ronaldinho. center, is introduced during his official presentation for Serie C soccer club Ravenna FC, Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026, in Ravenna, Italy. (AP Photo/Luca Bruno)

For more than a decade, Ronaldinho ’s playing career belonged to the past, even if his reputation as one of football’s most gifted entertainers never quite faded. When third-tier Italian club Ravenna announced his arrival in June, the prospect of seeing the Brazilian back in competitive action seemed more like an elaborate publicity exercise than a serious sporting proposition. On Sunday, at 46, he walked out in a No. 10 shirt and made it real.Ronaldinho started Ravenna’s Serie C derby against Forlì on November 15, playing the first 45 minutes of a 2-0 victory at the Stadio Bruno Benelli. It was his first appearance in a competitive professional match since leaving Fluminense in 2015, bringing an 11-year absence from the game to an end.The occasion was considerably larger than an ordinary third-tier fixture. Ravenna’s usual 5,000-capacity ground had been expanded with a temporary stand accommodating another 1,800 spectators, named “R10” in honour of the Brazilian. Flares and smoke bombs filled the stands as Andrea Bocelli’splayed over the stadium speakers, while Ronaldinho entered to a reception befitting a player whose influence on football extended far beyond the clubs he represented.Wearing Ravenna’s No. 10, the 2005 Ballon d’Or winner showed flashes of the close control and technical quality that defined his career. He did not score, nor did he create a clear opportunity for himself, but he was involved in the move that produced the opening goal.Giulio Donati put Ravenna ahead in the 36th minute with a strike from outside the penalty area, after Ronaldinho had helped set the attacking sequence in motion.He finished his half with 28 touches and an 81 per cent passing accuracy before acknowledging the supporters and making way for Matteo Maggio at the interval. Simone Rabbi added Ravenna’s second goal after the break to complete the 2-0 win.Ronaldinho had initially been expected to play around 30 minutes, but instead completed the entire first half. His contribution was necessarily limited by the circumstances of his return, yet the occasion was never solely about what he could produce over 90 minutes. Ravenna had brought one of football’s most recognisable figures back into a professional dressing room, and the response inside the Bruno Benelli showed what that meant to the club and its supporters.Speaking to Sky Italia afterwards, Ronaldinho said: “It went by too fast, that has always been football for me. Is this my last one? I don’t know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.“It was lovely to be here, playing, having the buildup in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.”Ravenna’s announcement in June was initially met with considerable scepticism. Ronaldinho had not played professional football since his departure from Fluminense in 2015 and formally announced his retirement in 2018, aged 37. The idea that he would resume his playing career more than a decade after his last competitive appearance, particularly with a club in Italy’s third division, was difficult for many to take seriously.The move was driven by Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani, who had bought his hometown club in June 2024. His stated ambition was to “make young people of Ravenna fall in love with football”, and signing a player he had grown up idolising offered an unusually direct way of pursuing it.Cipriani had made no secret of the fact that he wanted Ronaldinho to appear in the derby against Forlì. The Brazilian’s debut in that fixture had been the president’s dream from the beginning, and the match provided the occasion around which the club could build its return.The two men had developed a genuine friendship after being introduced by Lorenzo Tonetti, the former co-owner of Milan’s well-known Giannino restaurant, which Ronaldinho frequented during his time at AC Milan between July 2008 and January 2011. That relationship helped turn what might otherwise have remained an unlikely proposal into an agreement.Cipriani explained his admiration for the Brazilian in an interview with, saying: “I don't think there’s any other player who inspires such a love for the game as Ronaldinho does.”He also described the player's response when the possibility of returning to the pitch was raised. “That’s just how things go with Ronnie,” Cipriani told. “If there's a chance to have fun and excite people, he's all in.”Ronaldinho agreed immediately, according to Cipriani, and the arrangement extended beyond a one-off appearance. The former Barcelona and Brazil star also became a shareholder in Ravenna, giving him a stake in the club he had joined as a player. His arrival was facilitated by Cipriani, with the president's personal connection to the Brazilian central to bringing the deal together.Ronaldinho arrived in Ravenna on Friday and trained with the squad for the first time on Saturday, before being named in the starting line-up for the derby the following day. The short preparation period did little to diminish the anticipation surrounding his appearance.Ronaldinho’s return to Italy carried an additional connection to the country where he had already enjoyed one of the most memorable periods of his career. He represented AC Milan from July 2008 until January 2011, scoring his first goal in Italian football in a derby against Inter on September 28, 2008.That match was another occasion on which the Brazilian left his mark on a local rivalry, although the circumstances of Sunday's appearance were very different. At Milan, he was an established star competing at the highest level of European football. At Ravenna, he was returning at 46 to a club whose ambitions are centred on climbing the Italian divisions.Ravenna have not played in Serie B since 2008 and have never appeared in Serie A. They entered the weekend second in their Serie C regional group, with 29 points from 13 matches, while Forlì were 15th with 15 points. Ravenna had been reported to be six points behind leaders Spezia ahead of the fixture.The result preserved Ravenna’s position near the top of the table, but the larger significance of the derby was the fulfilment of a project that had seemed improbable when it was first announced. Ronaldinho's presence brought attention to a club competing outside Italy's top two divisions, while giving supporters an opportunity to see a player whose career had helped define an era of attacking football.Whether Sunday's appearance becomes a regular feature remains uncertain. Ronaldinho has not committed to a schedule of further matches, but his comments after the game left the possibility open. His willingness to return whenever Cipriani asks suggests that the derby may not necessarily be the only time he wears Ravenna's No. 10.
Article Summary: Ronaldinho returns after 11 years as Ravenna beat Forlì in local derby. Ronaldinho played the first 45 minutes of a 2-0 victory at the Stadio Bruno Benelli. Ravenna’s usual 5,000-capacity ground had been expanded with a temporary stand accommodating another 1,800 spectators.

Article Title: ‘He got greedy’: Ex-India captain's blunt take on Arshdeep Singh after four-wicket haul

Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in Auckland, but believes the left-arm pacer could have avoided an expensive finish to his spell.India began their five-match ODI series with a comfortable win at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. In a rain-interrupted contest reduced to 32 overs per side, New Zealand were bowled out for 185 before India chased down the revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs. Virat Kohli led the chase with a fluent 74, while Shubman Gill contributed 37 as the duo stitched together a 113-run partnership. India eventually crossed the finish line with five wickets to spare and 56 deliveries remaining.With the ball, Arshdeep was India's leading wicket-taker, claiming four wickets in his 10 overs. However, his figures of 4/70 were inflated by an expensive final over in which New Zealand tailender Blair Tickner struck him for three sixes, taking 23 runs off the over.Assessing the pacer's performance, Jadeja felt Arshdeep had been impressive for most of his spell but allowed the opportunity to complete a five-wicket haul to influence his bowling towards the end."I would call him slightly greedy. He himself said that as well. If you remove his last over, he had dismissed four batters before that and had given 40-odd runs. He got slightly greedy for the fifth wicket in the last over," Jadeja said on Sony Sports Network.Arshdeep had himself admitted after the match that the fifth wicket would have been his favourite, indicating that he was keen to complete a five-wicket haul. Despite missing out on the milestone, his four-wicket effort placed him in an exclusive group of Indian fast bowlers to achieve the feat in an ODI in New Zealand, alongside Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami.Jadeja, however, stressed that the expensive final over should not overshadow what Arshdeep brings to India's bowling combination. He pointed to the value of having a left-arm fast bowler in an attack that already features Jasprit Bumrah, adding that the competition for places would only benefit the team."It happens. It's natural, but Arshdeep Singh is showing that he can play in ODIs as well, which I believe is a very good thing when a left-arm seamer gets added to this attack with (Jasprit) Bumrah. The competition has increased a lot, which is very good for India," Jadeja elaborated.Jadeja also reserved praise for Anshul Kamboj, who delivered an economical spell of 2/22 from his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award.The former India batter acknowledged that Kamboj had faced questions over his bowling during his Test debut against England in 2025, particularly regarding his pace and tendency to bowl no-balls. However, he felt the youngster had shown considerable improvement in Auckland.Jadeja also suggested that Kamboj's workload before the England assignment could have contributed to his struggles, pointing out that fatigue can affect a bowler's execution. His performance against New Zealand, according to Jadeja, reflected better pace, consistency and accuracy."He bowled extremely well. The vision everyone had was that he didn't have pace when he played in England and was bowling a lot of no-balls. I think he had come after playing a lot of cricket then. So a guy also gets tired. It's not that easy. Then he was playing for the first time, but the consistency and the slight increase in his pace he showed today (Wednesday), if we talk about the accuracy amongst the four bowlers, it's Anshul Kamboj," Jadeja added.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by five wickets in the first ODI in Auckland. Ajay Jadeja praised Arshdeep Singh's performance, but said he could have avoided expensive final over. Jadeja also praised Anshul Kamboj's bowling, saying he had shown improvement.

Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has revealed details of an awkward conversation with Steve Smith before publishing his claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in his autobiography, Sabr.Khawaja said he waited until Smith had finished playing a Test match in South Africa before speaking to him about the book.Speaking on the They Used To Be... podcast, Khawaja said he had spoken to several players connected to the controversy before making his account public."Steven Smith was a bit more awkward, he was playing in that Test. I waited until it finished and I talked to him," Khawaja said.He also revealed that Cameron Bancroft , who was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball during the Cape Town Test, contacted him before the book was published."Obviously it came out in the media I talked to Patty, so I'm happy with that and I talked to Davey and Bancroft reached out to me and I have had a lot of conversations with him," he said.Khawaja said his conversation with Smith came years after another exchange in which the former Australia captain had persuaded him not to speak publicly on his own.He said he had wanted to address the issue as a team from the beginning but was talked out of speaking independently."It's not what I wanted, but I felt that right from the very start I gave an account of me wanting to take it as a team... wanting to come out, but being talked out of coming out by myself from Steven Smith and then wanting to come out in 2021."Smith and David Warner were banned for 12 months by Cricket Australia following the 2018 Cape Town Test. India's batting collapse in the fourth ODI against New Zealand has prompted serious questions about the team's approach, with head coach Gautam Gambhir expressing concern over repeated failures and former India opener Aakash Chopra backing his call for greater responsibility from the batters.India endured a disastrous start to their 334-run chase at Mount Maunganui on Friday, losing Rohit Sharma , Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer without scoring by the end of the opening over. Another wicket fell before the end of the sixth over, and the visitors eventually crumbled to 89, suffering a humiliating 244-run defeat. It was India's second-heaviest loss in ODI cricket.Chopra, analysing the defeat on ESPNcricinfo, echoed Gambhir's assessment that the Indian batters needed to show greater application rather than surrender against quality bowling."As Gautam Gambhir mentioned after the match, there are no unplayable deliveries in the game of cricket. Yes, it was great bowling, but you need to be better. And that's the way to look at it. You can't completely surrender. You have to find a way. It's just that it happened so quickly that you really didn't have the time to recover, regroup, reassess and play differently," Aakash Chopra said.Much of India's misery was orchestrated by Matt Henry , who dismantled the top order before completing a six-wicket haul.The New Zealand fast bowler returned figures of 9.4-2-27-6, leaving the Indian batters struggling to cope with his movement and accuracy.Chopra pointed out that Henry's effectiveness increases considerably in the longer white-ball format, particularly when conditions offer assistance to the new ball."He didn't look as menacing in the T20Is. But the moment the format gets longer, there are two new balls, and there's a bit in the surface, that's when Matt Henry becomes a very difficult bowler to negotiate early on when the ball is new. Pakistan legend Wasim Akram has questioned Pat Cummins ' claim that he had no knowledge of the ball-tampering incident during the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test, arguing that an experienced bowler would immediately recognise if sandpaper had been used on the ball.The Sandpapergate controversy has returned to the spotlight following Usman Khawaja 's explosive claims in his book, Sabr, that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper. With David Warner backing Khawaja and Cummins strongly rejecting the allegations, the row shows little sign of dying down.Akram, one of the finest exponents of reverse swing, weighed in on the debate, explaining why the scratches caused by sandpaper would be noticeably different from the marks produced through conventional ball maintenance.Akram said he was surprised by Cummins' statement, given his role as a bowler during the Cape Town Test."I saw Pat Cummins, who's a very close friend of mine, a great cricket er and one of the top leaders in world cricket, saying that he didn't know. So probably the team didn't know at the time what was happening, in my opinion. It's my opinion. It can be right or wrong."But as a bowler, when the cricket ball comes in my hand, either it's the fifth over, either it's in the 10th over, or either it's in the 50th over, the old ball, where you look after the ball, you shine the one side; if it's a dry day, dry square, you one bounce throw, you get scratch a bit.But the sandpaper scratch is totally different from the one-bounce scratch," Akram said in a video posted on social media.The former Pakistan captain challenged cricket fans to examine the difference themselves by rubbing sandpaper on a semi-new ball."And as a cricket lover, if you want to check, grab a semi-new cricket ball, grab a piece of sandpaper, and rub it in; you know, the scratches are totally different," he said.Akram clarified that he was not taking sides in the dispute but stressed that honesty was central to Australia's cricketing reputation."So again, as I said, I'm not taking anybody's sides. And Australians are known and famous for their straightforwardness, hardness on the field, off the field, and most importantly, honesty. And I think that's what the whole nation has been, you know, under stress a bit, obviously, eight years ago and back to it again. I hope things get sorted out," he added.He reiterated his belief that an experienced bowler would recognise unusual damage to the ball."This is my take on this issue: as a bowler, especially an experienced bowler, I'll have a look at the ball, and I'll know straight away something is not right," he concluded.Cummins has firmly rejected Khawaja's suggestion that the entire Australian side knew about the sandpaper plan."When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong," Cummins said."I've said that consistently for the last eight years, I did not know that was happening. But I think Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that. He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball-tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense. I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam (Bancroft) to be careful when using sandpaper," he added.With Warner continuing to support Khawaja, former Australia captain Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft also part of the original sanctions, and questions now being raised by Akram, the controversy sparked by Khawaja's revelations looks far from over.
Article Summary: Wasim Akram questions Pat Cummins' claim that he had no knowledge of the ball- tampering incident during the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test. Akram argues that an experienced bowler would immediately recognise if sandpaper had been used on the ball. The former Pakistan captain challenged cricket fans to examine the difference themselves by rubbing sandpaper on a semi-new ball.

Article Title: 'Are we in kindergarten?': Ex-India spinner backs Khawaja, tears into Cummins' sandpapergate explanation

Former India spinner Murali Kartik has backed Usman Khawaja in the ongoing debate over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning Pat Cummins ' claim that he was unaware of the plan to use sandpaper during the Cape Town Test against South Africa.The controversy resurfaced after Khawaja made several claims in his memoir, Sabr, suggesting that the entire Australian team, including current Test captain Cummins, knew about the plan to alter the condition of the ball.Cummins rejected the allegations during a press conference on Friday, describing Khawaja's claims as "complete and utter nonsense".Kartik, however, sided with Khawaja and said it was difficult to believe that the bowlers were unaware of a plan that was allegedly being carried out for their benefit."When it happened, there was a mini probe and three players were sent to the galley. Once that is happening, and if I am the bowler while the other two guys are doing it for me, I don't know how anyone can say that I didn't know about it. How can anyone say that?" Kartik said on Cricbuzz.He also questioned why only three players were held responsible for the incident, arguing that the bowlers would have been informed if the plan was intended to help them."I was surprised that only three guys had to bear the brunt of it. Warner is going to tell the story once he is done with everything. ' It's not him, it's Usman Khawaja who has come out and said that everybody knew. Warner subsequently accused the Australia captain of throwing his close friend Khawaja "under the bus".

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again
Article Text:
Sumit Antil and Pranav Soorma (ANI/PTI Photo)

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

Pranav Soorma defends club throw crown

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep at the Asian Para Games. Pranav Soorma defends his title in the men's club throw F51 event. Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar complete all-Indian podium finish.

Mona's record-breaking run in shooting

Nishad's golden double in athletics

NEW DELHI: Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics.Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump.Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close.The 38-year-old Mona opened India's medal account in shooting by winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games-record score of 250.0 points. Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events.
