Article Title: Jesús de Miguel’s family receive €217,895 after football community rallies behind crowdfunding campaign following striker’s death
Article Text:
Jesus de Miguel (Pic credit: Tenerife)

Jesús de Miguel’s family thank donors as crowdfunding campaign raises €217,895

Soccer Football - Funeral of CD Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel - Navahermosa, Spain - November 5, 2026 Mourners carry the coffin of Jesus de Miguel as they head towards the cemetery for the funeral REUTERS/Alejandro Martinez Velez

What happened to Jesús de Miguel during Tenerife vs Andorra?

CD Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel reacts after a collision with FC Andorra's Jesus Owono, Soccer Football, LaLiga 2, CD Tenerife v FC Andorra, Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez, Santa Cruz de Tenerife,

Jesús Owono handed 12-match suspension after fatal collision

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The family of Jesús de Miguel have received an extraordinary show of support following the death of the Spanish striker during a match between CD Tenerife and FC Andorra. A crowdfunding campaign launched by fellow footballer Fran Sol has raised more than €217,000, with donations arriving from players, club executives and supporters. The family have now publicly acknowledged the contributions, while the goalkeeper involved in the fatal collision has been handed a 12-match suspension.The family of Jesús de Miguel have confirmed that they have received the donations collected through a crowdfunding campaign launched by footballer Fran Sol, following the striker’s death on November 3.In a statement published by the Spanish players’ association AFE, the family expressed their gratitude to everyone who had contributed, describing the response as a source of comfort during an extremely difficult period.“We have already received the donations from the crowdfunding campaign launched by the footballer Fran Sol, and we would like to express our deepest thanks and gratitude to everyone for this outpouring of love and support that we have received,” the statement read.The family also acknowledged the scale of the response, saying they had been moved by the number of people who had rallied behind the initiative.“We have been deeply moved to see such a large number of people rally around this initiative.Every kind gesture means a great deal to us, and we want you to know that we have received all these kind sentiments with the utmost love”.They added that messages of support had carried particular significance for relatives still trying to come to terms with the loss.“We extend our deepest thanks to everyone who contributed with their kind messages, in words that seemed simple yet carried every meaning of gratitude for a family still living through the impact of the shock, and trying to find some comfort in the solidarity of the thousands around them”.The campaign remains open. As of November 14, it had raised €217,895 towards its €300,000 target, with approximately 5,400 donations recorded. That represents more than 72 per cent of the intended amount, and the total may continue to increase as contributions arrive.Several prominent figures from Spanish football were among the donors. Cádiz president Cristian Siptin contributed €15,000, while Ceuta president Luhay Hamido donated €3,500. Players also supported the campaign, with Pedro Porro giving €3,500 and Marc Bartra contributing €3,000. Alex Remiro and Borja Iglesias each donated €2,500.The tragedy occurred on Monday, November 2, during a Segunda División fixture between CD Tenerife and FC Andorra. The match was level at 2-2 when De Miguel attempted to challenge for a high ball and collided with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, who had come out of his goal to deal with the situation.The collision left the Tenerife striker suffering a cardiac arrest, bringing the match to a halt as medical staff rushed to provide emergency treatment on the pitch. Players and spectators watched as medical personnel attempted to revive him, while the incident left both teams visibly shaken.Owono, the Equatorial Guinea international, received a straight red card for the challenge. De Miguel was given immediate medical assistance before being taken for further treatment, but his death was announced the following day, November 3.The incident prompted an outpouring of grief across Spanish football, with the fundraising campaign becoming one of the ways players and supporters could help his family.Owono subsequently expressed his devastation over what had happened, acknowledging the pain of losing the striker and the suffering of those closest to him.“These are the hardest days of my life. I find it extremely difficult to express my feelings, and I am unable to come to terms with what happened. I feel great pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family and of everyone who loved him,” he said.The goalkeeper also recognised that there would be matters to address following the incident, but said his immediate thoughts remained with De Miguel and his family.“I know there are many matters that must be dealt with, and I will face everything that comes with the utmost respect. But right now, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are living through. Rest in peace, Jesus”.The disciplinary consequences of the incident have now been confirmed, with the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) handing Owono a 12-match suspension on Friday, November 13.The maximum sanction follows the collision during the November 2 fixture, when the 25-year-old goalkeeper rushed out of his area and struck De Miguel while attempting to defend the ball. The suspension represents a significant sporting penalty for Owono, who will be unavailable for FC Andorra for the duration of the ban.The decision comes less than two weeks after the incident, which has left both clubs and the wider Spanish football community mourning De Miguel.For De Miguel's family, the donations have provided tangible support at a time when they continue to live with the loss. The campaign launched by Sol remains open, and the €300,000 target has yet to be reached, despite contributions from thousands of people across the game.
Article Summary: Jesús de Miguel died following a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono on November 3. A crowdfunding campaign launched by fellow footballer Fran Sol has raised more than €217,000, with donations arriving from players, club executives and supporters. De Miguel's family have now publicly acknowledged the contributions. The goalkeeper involved in the fatal collision has been handed a 12-match suspension.

Article Title: India look to bounce back from humiliating 0-5 defeat against New Zealand as Khalid Jamil demands greater accountability
Article Text:
India head coach Khalid Jamil (Image: ANI)

Khalid Jamil demands accountability after Auckland defeat

Anirudh Thapa calls for discipline and better communication

Four debutants feature as India continue rebuilding process

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Indian men's football team faces a crucial opportunity to restore some pride when it takes on New Zealand in the second of their two international friendlies at the newly opened One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch on Sunday. Stung by a crushing 0-5 defeat in Auckland, the Blue Tigers will be eager to deliver a stronger performance and show signs of improvement against the hosts.The match, scheduled to kick off at 8:40 AM IST, will also mark the first-ever international football fixture at the 25,000-capacity One New Zealand Stadium, a fully roofed venue in the heart of Christchurch.The multi-purpose stadium, which opened in March this year, is situated on land named Te Kaha, while the wider precinct is known as Te Kaharoa, meaning 'Enduring Strength' in Māori, according to the All India Football Federation (AIFF).India head coach Khalid Jamil has urged his players to take responsibility and correct their mistakes after a disappointing outing in the opening fixture. New Zealand, ranked 88th in the world, exposed India's defensive vulnerabilities, scoring five goals through a Bijoy Varghese own goal, a brace from Jesse Randall, and strikes from Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss.Acknowledging the gulf in quality between the two sides, Jamil insisted that there could be no excuses for the result and called for a determined response."If you see the result, it was not up to the mark, but the players are giving their best. The attitude of the players has been very good. We were playing against a stronger team, no doubt, but there is no excuse. We need to rectify our mistakes and fight back. In tomorrow's game, every player must take responsibility and give everything," Jamil said.The Indian coach also highlighted the difficulties surrounding the team's preparations, particularly the long-distance travel and limited time to adapt to the conditions before the first match."We also need to note the external factors beyond our control. We are playing an away game, and there is a seven-and-a-half-hour time difference. We had only one day of practice before travelling, and then had to play within two days. It takes time to adjust. Sometimes the mind is ready, but the body is not. But now everybody is settled, I believe," he added.Taking responsibility for the heavy defeat, Jamil admitted that both individual errors and his own decisions contributed to the outcome. However, he remained encouraged by the players' attitude and determination to improve."The result, yes, it is my mistake. There were individual errors as well that led to the goals we conceded. But one good thing is the attitude of the players. They are ready to bounce back," he said.India captain Anirudh Thapa also acknowledged the disappointment within the dressing room after the Auckland defeat, stressing that the team must learn from its mistakes and show greater discipline in Christchurch.The 28-year-old, who captained India for only the second time in his international career during the opening fixture, said New Zealand capitalised on India's mistakes and underlined the need for a collective response."It was a very disappointing result for us. The boys were devastated after the game. We came here wanting to put in a good performance, but New Zealand were strong and punished our mistakes. We have to take responsibility as a team. We know we can do better, and we have to show that tomorrow," Thapa said."At this level, you cannot afford to make too many mistakes. We have to be more disciplined, stay compact and communicate better with each other."Thapa also emphasised the importance of keeping the squad united during difficult moments, adding that leadership must come from every player on the pitch."For me, it is about keeping everyone together. When things are not going well, we have to support each other and keep pushing. If I am given the captaincy, I have to lead by example, but every player has a responsibility towards the team and the country," he added.The Blue Tigers travelled to Christchurch on Friday evening after holding a gym session in the morning for players who had not completed the full 90 minutes in Auckland. The team subsequently held its official training session at One New Zealand Stadium on Saturday, completing preparations for the second friendly.India handed international debuts to four players in the opening fixture — Muhammad Suhail, David Lalhlansanga, Tomba Singh Haobam and Ricky Meetei Haobam — as Jamil continues to provide opportunities to new faces while building towards the team's future.The head coach has also urged supporters to remain patient with the team's development, insisting that matches against stronger opposition are important for the players' growth."For the fans and everyone, they have to be patient. The players are thinking positively, and we are trying to build ahead. When we are down, we want the fans to support us. We are in a good process, and we need to play these kinds of matches. We are also giving opportunities to new faces," Jamil said.Despite the disappointing start to the tour, the coach insisted that his players were motivated to make amends in Christchurch."We have to bounce back tomorrow. I will not leave anything in this game. We have to give everything. I have already given the message to the players. We have to go out and give everything. They are highly motivated," he said.Thapa echoed those sentiments, describing the second fixture as an opportunity for India to respond positively rather than dwell on the previous result."We have another opportunity here in Christchurch, and we have to make the most of it. We cannot change the past result, but we can learn from it. We want to put in a much better performance," the India captain said.
Article Summary: India take on New Zealand at the newly opened One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch on Sunday. The match will mark the first-ever international football fixture at the 25,000-capacity venue in the heart of Christchurch. The Blue Tigers were beaten 0-5 by New Zealand in their opening fixture in Auckland. India handed debuts to four players in the opening fixture.

Article Title: Portugal plan special Ronaldo tribute: Entire squad to wear No. 7 shirts, Denmark game to pause in seventh minute
Article Text:
FILE - Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo prepares to kick a penalty during a round of sixteen match between Portugal and Slovenia at the Euro 2024 soccer tournament in Frankfurt, Germany, Monday, July 1, 2024. (AP Photo/Matthias Schrader, File)

Portugal players to wear Cristiano Ronaldo's No. 7 shirt against Denmark

Jorge Jesus explains who organised Portugal's farewell to Ronaldo

Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal records after 23 years and 146 goals

FILE - Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo gestures as he holds the trophy while celebrating winning the UEFA Nations League final soccer match between Portugal and Netherlands at the Dragao stadium in Porto, Portugal. AP/PTI(AP11_05_2026_000313B)

Portugal are preparing a series of tributes to Cristiano Ronaldo when they face Denmark in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday, marking the end of an international career that lasted more than two decades. The Portuguese Football Federation has approved a collective gesture involving every player in the squad, while supporters at the Estadio Municipal de Braga will also have an opportunity to honour their former captain during the match.The most visible part of the tribute will come before kick-off, when every member of Portugal's squad is expected to wear the No. 7 shirt associated with Ronaldo as the team walks out at the Estadio Municipal de Braga.The decision was reportedly finalised during a meeting on Thursday involving Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proença, national team head coach Jorge Jesus and the senior leadership group. The players involved in the discussions included captains Bernardo Silva, Rúben Dias and Bruno Fernandes.According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola , the meeting brought together the federation's leadership and coaching staff to determine how best to recognise Ronaldo's contribution following his announcement of international retirement on November 5.The tribute will extend beyond the pre-match walk-out. The match is also scheduled to be paused in the seventh minute, allowing supporters to rise and applaud the former captain. UEFA has reportedly granted special permission for the gesture, giving fans at the Braga stadium an opportunity to recognise the player whose number has become synonymous with Portuguese football.Ronaldo's attendance remains unconfirmed, so it is not yet clear whether he will be present to witness the ceremony himself.Jesus addressed the arrangements during his pre-match press conference, making clear that the tribute was a decision taken by the federation rather than one organised independently by the coaching staff.“Such decisions are always the responsibility of the Portuguese Football Federation, more specifically its football and sporting departments and its president,” Jesus said.The Portugal coach also spoke about the scale of Ronaldo's contribution, pointing to the 23 years he spent representing the national team and the influence he had beyond the country.“It is brilliant because nobody can forget the 23 years Cris spent with the national team, what he achieved for Portugal, and the impact he has had on the world of football,” Jesus added.The federation has also decided to leave vacant the room Ronaldo used at Cidade do Futebol, Portugal's national team training complex. The gesture is intended to preserve a symbolic place for the former captain within the squad during the first international break following his retirement.The arrangements come as Portugal begin preparing for a future without the player who has been central to their national team for much of the modern era. Bruno Fernandes and Bernardo Silva are among the experienced figures expected to assume greater leadership responsibilities, although Ronaldo's departure leaves a significant gap in both the squad's history and its attacking record.Ronaldo retired from international football with 146 goals in 234 appearances, records that leave him as the leading goalscorer and most-capped player in the history of men's international football.His Portugal debut came on August 20, 2003, against Kazakhstan, beginning a career that concluded on September 24, 2026. Across those 23 years, he became the defining figure of a generation that delivered the country's first European Championship title and two Nations League triumphs.Portugal's victory at Euro 2016 in France was the defining achievement of Ronaldo's international career, followed by Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025. His individual records extended across both major international competitions: he scored 11 goals in 27 World Cup appearances, making him Portugal's leading scorer at the tournament, and established the men's record of 14 goals in European Championship final tournaments.He also became the only player to score at six different men's World Cups, finding the net in Germany in 2006, South Africa in 2010, Brazil in 2014, Russia in 2018, Qatar in 2022 and the 2026 tournament. His combined total of 25 goals across the European Championship and World Cup is another men's international record.Ronaldo scored against 49 different national teams, with Luxembourg conceding 11 goals and Hungary nine. His international record also includes 10 hat-tricks, two of which contained four goals, and 22 converted penalties. Of his 146 goals, 124 came in competitive internationals, excluding friendly matches.Those numbers provide the statistical measure of a career that also included unsuccessful campaigns and difficult tournament exits before Portugal's major successes. The tribute against Denmark will give the federation, the players and supporters an opportunity to recognise the full contribution of a footballer whose influence extended well beyond the records he accumulated.
Article Summary: Portugal preparing a series of tributes to Cristiano Ronaldo when they face Denmark in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday. The Portuguese Football Federation has approved a collective gesture involving every player in the squad. The most visible part of the tribute will come before kick-off, when every member of Portugal's squad is expected to wear the No. 7 shirt associated with Ronaldo. UEFA has reportedly granted special permission for the gesture. The match is also scheduled to be paused in the seventh minute, allowing supporters to rise and applaud the former captain.

Article Title: Jesus Owono handed 12-match ban after Jesus de Miguel's death; FC Andorra goalkeeper yet to decide on return
Article Text:
Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono (AP Photo)

Owono yet to decide on return after 'most difficult days of my life'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tribute to CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel. (Reuters Photo)

De Miguel's family thanks supporters after fundraising campaign

Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match suspension by the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee following the on-field collision that led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.Owono, who plays for Spanish second-division club FC Andorra, collided with De Miguel during their league match on November 2. The Tenerife forward was rushed to hospital and admitted to intensive care but died the following day.The federation's disciplinary committee imposed the maximum sanction under Article 102 of the Royal Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary code, which deals with violent conduct against an opponent during play resulting in serious injury. The suspension also carries the associated fines prescribed under Article 52."The referee's own description makes it possible to appreciate the particular seriousness of the action, both because of the way it was carried out, with the leg raised, and because of the forcefulness of the impact, which the referee expressly described as excessive," the committee said."It is public knowledge that the tragic outcome of the events was the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," it added, saying that the particular seriousness of the case justified "the imposition of the sanction at its maximum level".While the disciplinary action has now been announced, Owono's immediate future in football remains uncertain, with the 25-year-old yet to decide when, or whether, he will return to competitive action.FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said on Thursday that the club would give the goalkeeper the time and space needed to make that decision following the tragedy."What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to him," Manso said at a press conference on Thursday."We will give him space so that he feels completely free to make any decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return."Manso added that Owono was spending time with his family, friends and partner as he dealt with the aftermath of the incident."It is a very complicated situation to manage," the manager said, adding that the goalkeeper would decide his next step "when he feels it is appropriate and when he feels genuinely ready to take a decision like that".Owono had earlier withdrawn from Equatorial Guinea's squad for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe this month. The goalkeeper, who has 47 international caps, had described the ordeal as "the most difficult days of my life" in a statement released through his club.The Equatorial Guinea Football Federation also said he was experiencing profound sorrow and grief following De Miguel's death.Meanwhile, De Miguel's family issued a statement on Thursday through the Spanish Players Association, thanking those who had extended their support following the Tenerife forward's death.A crowdfunding campaign organised by third-tier club Hercules forward Fran Sol for the family had raised €213,160."We would like to express our heartfelt thanks for all the expressions of affection and support we have received," De Miguel's family said."We have been deeply moved to see so many of you rally behind this initiative."The family also thanked Sol for setting up the campaign, with the proceeds intended to support De Miguel's relatives.FC Andorra are scheduled to travel to Almeria on Saturday for their first fixture since the tragedy.
Article Summary: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed 12-match suspension by Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee. Owono collided with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel during their league match on November 2. De Miguel was taken to hospital but died the following day. The suspension carries the associated fines prescribed under Article 52.

Article Title: No number 10 jersey, stands not full: Messi-less Argentina brought down to earth by Uruguay
Article Text:
Lionel Messi

Argentina's first match in the post-Lionel Messi era ended in defeat, with Uruguay beating the world champions 2-1 in an international friendly at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires on Friday.Playing their first match since Messi's retirement from international football in early October, Argentina were unable to begin the new chapter with a win under coach Lionel Scaloni.Uruguay took the lead in the 48th minute through an own goal by Leonardo Balerdi. Five minutes later, Maximiliano Araújo doubled the visitors' advantage under new coach Diego Forlán.Julián Álvarez pulled one back for Argentina in the 73rd minute, but the hosts could not find an equaliser.The match, known as the clásico rioplatense, marked the beginning of a new phase for Argentina following Messi's international retirement. Scaloni, who led the team to the 2022 FIFA World Cup title, extended his contract until 2030 earlier this week.Messi's absence was the biggest talking point ahead of the match. The 39-year-old brought an end to his international career last month after an emotional farewell friendly against Benin, having represented Argentina in 207 matches and scored 125 goals.The impact of his absence was also visible in the stands, with La Bombonera falling short of a sellout crowd, something rarely seen during Argentina matches.Although most supporters wore Argentina's traditional blue-and-white jersey with Messi's No. 10 on the back, Scaloni decided not to give the shirt number to another player. The coach said he was yet to decide who would succeed Messi and preferred to leave the number vacant for now, as there was no obligation to assign it.On the field, Argentina continued to dominate possession but lacked the attacking threat and creativity that Messi brought to the team in the final third. Neither Nicolás Paz nor Thiago Almada managed to fill that gap.Argentina will look to return to winning ways when they face Costa Rica in Córdoba on Tuesday. Uruguay, meanwhile, will host the Dominican Republic on the same day.
Article Summary: Argentina's first match in the post-Lionel Messi era ended in defeat. Uruguay beat the world champions 2-1 in an international friendly at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires on Friday. Lionel Messi retired from international football in early October.

Article Title: Barcelona offer fans worldwide chance to have loved ones’ ashes permanently preserved at Camp Nou for €10,000 as stadium revamp bill soars to €2bn
Article Text:
Barcelona’s renovated Camp Nou will feature 26,000 memorial spaces, allowing fans worldwide to honour loved ones with permanent resting places at the stadium/ Image: Barca

Barcelona plan 26,000 niches in new Camp Nou memorial

Poll Vote & Share your view Would you consider purchasing a niche for a loved one in the Camp Nou memorial? Yes, definitely. No, I wouldn't. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

How much will it cost to have ashes placed at Camp Nou?

Camp Nou redevelopment continues as costs approach €2 billion

Barcelona supporters will soon be able to maintain their connection with the club long after their deaths, with the renovated Camp Nou set to include a dedicated memorial where families can place the ashes of loved ones. The project will offer 26,000 spaces for funeral urns, alongside commemorative plaques, allowing supporters from around the world to secure a place at the stadium without needing to be club members. The privilege, however, comes with a range of fees and time-limited concessions.The club's Memorial FC Barcelona will occupy a 1,500-square-metre space within Camp Nou, combining a columbarium with an area for commemorative plaques. A columbarium is a dedicated structure containing individual compartments, known as niches, in which funeral urns holding cremated remains can be placed.Designed by architect Quique Montoya, the memorial is being developed in collaboration with the company Mes Que Un Memorial. Its design will feature four large illuminated squares, with urns housed behind a mural depicting significant moments from Barcelona's 125-year history.Commemorative plaques will be displayed on a glass wall illuminated by LED lighting.The club has described the interior as a contemporary space using fine materials and warm lighting, with large murals and visual, audiovisual and sound installations dedicated to its history. Families will be able to choose between placing a loved one's ashes in a niche or having their name and a personal message displayed on a plaque.Both options will be available to Barcelona supporters worldwide, regardless of whether they hold club membership. Concessions will be offered for 10, 25 or 50 years, while a separate option will allow supporters to secure a niche permanently.The cost of a place in the columbarium will depend on the length of the concession. A 10-year arrangement is priced at €2,490 (approximately $2,753), while a 50-year concession will cost €6,000 (approximately $6,634). An annual maintenance fee of €70 (around $77) will also apply.Supporters seeking a permanent resting place can purchase a niche for €10,000 (approximately $11,057). A commemorative plaque is available separately for €490 (around $542) for a standard 10-year arrangement, while a premium plaque lasting 50 years will cost €1,040.Barcelona said interest in the initiative had already come from supporters, club members, former players and relatives of historic figures associated with the institution. More than 1,000 fans have reportedly booked places ahead of the memorial's opening, with their contributions also expected to help fund the stadium redevelopment.Presenting the project, the club's institutional vice-president, María Elena Fort, explained the personal attachment that had inspired the idea. “When my grandfather died many years ago, he said the only thing he wanted was to be buried next to Barça’s pitch so that he could hear the goals go in during the afterlife. Many fans dream of the same thing,” she said.Barcelona are not the first Spanish club to introduce such a facility. Atlético Madrid, Real Betis and Espanyol already have smaller columbaria at their respective stadiums.The memorial forms part of Barcelona's wider modernisation of Camp Nou, a stadium originally built in 1957. The redevelopment began in 2023, with the club aiming to increase capacity from 99,354 to 105,000, making it Europe's largest football stadium and the second largest in the world, behind the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea.The project has faced delays and substantial cost increases. Initially estimated at €900 million (approximately $996 million), the redevelopment bill has since risen to nearly €2 billion (approximately $2.2 billion). The financial burden has also affected supporters, with ticket prices having doubled in recent years for non-season-ticket holders.Barcelona have already returned to their home ground, although its capacity remains restricted while construction of the upper tier continues. The club will have to leave the stadium temporarily again next season while the roof is installed. Once completed, Camp Nou is expected to accommodate 105,000 spectators.The memorial is being developed in two phases, with construction scheduled to begin in late 2027 and the full project expected to be completed by the middle of 2028. The completed stadium is also among three venues being considered to host the 2034 World Cup final, which Spain, Portugal and Morocco are due to co-host. Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu and the Grand Stade Hassan II, under construction near Casablanca with a planned capacity of 115,000, are the other candidates.
Article Summary: Barcelona's renovated Camp Nou will feature 26,000 memorial spaces. The project will offer fans worldwide to honour loved ones with permanent resting places at the stadium. The privilege, however, comes with a range of fees and time-limited concessions. More than 1,000 fans have reportedly booked places ahead of the memorial's opening.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s eldest son nearly scores on Portugal U17 debut in 4-0 win over Andorra, days after father’s international retirement

Ronaldo Jr. begins new chapter one week after father's Portugal retirement

Cristiano Ronaldo’s international career may have reached its conclusion, but his family’s association with Portugal has entered a new chapter. His eldest son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. , made his Under-17 debut in a 4-0 victory over Andorra in European Championship qualifying on Thursday, coming close to marking his first appearance with a goal after entering the match in the closing stages.The 16-year-old came off the bench in the 74th minute at Portugal’s national training centre in Oeiras, replacing Victor Bastianele with the hosts already holding a commanding advantage. Wearing the number 18 shirt, Ronaldo Jr. was given an opportunity to make his first appearance at Under-17 level after previously representing Portugal at Under-15 and Under-16 age groups.Portugal had established their four-goal lead before his introduction in the second half. Sporting CP forward Diego Farinha scored twice, while Kauã Miranda converted a penalty for the third goal and Braga's Rafael Cabral added another in the 60th minute. Filipe Ramos' side secured a comfortable opening victory in their qualifying campaign for the 2027 European Under-17 Championship with an impressive attacking display.The occasion also attracted attention from Portugal's senior internationals. Vitinha, João Cancelo, João Félix and João Neves were among those watching from the sports complex in Oeiras as Ronaldo Jr. began his latest international assignment.Ronaldo Jr. nearly added a fifth goal in the closing stages, coming within inches of a memorable start to his Under-17 career. In the 88th minute, he connected with a cross from Diogo Djabi but sent his header narrowly wide of the goal.Although he could not find the net, the chance offered an early glimpse of his involvement at the new age level. He did not start the match and, unlike his father, did not wear Portugal's famous number seven shirt, instead appearing in number 18.The teenager arrived at the Under-17 level with an established record in Portugal's youth teams. His international journey began in May 2025, when he made his Under-15 debut wearing number seven at a tournament in Croatia. He subsequently represented the Under-16 side and helped Portugal win the Federation Cup in Turkey. Across his youth international appearances, he had scored five goals in 13 matches before making the step up.At club level, Ronaldo Jr. plays in the Al-Nassr academy in Saudi Arabia and has continued to attract attention with his performances, including a two-goal display against Al-Ahli earlier this season.The timing of the debut added another dimension to the occasion, coming just one week after his father announced his retirement from international football. Cristiano Ronaldo ended a 23-year Portugal career with a record 146 goals in 234 appearances, having represented the national team at the highest level since making his senior debut in 2003.Ronaldo Jr. now has the opportunity to establish his own place in Portugal's youth sides, with two further European Championship qualifiers scheduled during the current international window. Portugal are due to face Bulgaria on November 14 before meeting Serbia on November 17, with both matches taking place in Lisbon.The Andorra match was only his first appearance at Under-17 level, but the teenager will have further opportunities to gain experience as Portugal pursue qualification for the 2027 tournament.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. makes Portugal U17 debut against Andorra. The 16-year-old came off the bench in the 74th minute at Portugal’s national training centre in Oeiras. Diego Farinha scored twice, while Kauã Miranda converted a penalty for the third goal and Braga's Rafael Cabral added another in the 60th minute. Portugal secured a comfortable opening victory in their qualifying campaign for the 2027 European Under-17 Championship.
